# Cortonis Pharma — Deviation & CAPA Process Mining

> *Lyon's average step duration is in line with the network. Its CAPA cycle time is 40% longer. Standard reporting cannot explain the gap — process mining can.*

**All data in this repo is synthetic.** It's generated by [`data/generate_event_log.py`](data/generate_event_log.py) with a fixed random seed, no real company data is used anywhere. Cortonis Pharma is a made-up pharma company I use across a few of my portfolio projects — any resemblance to a real company is coincidental.

## Status

- [x] Phase 1 — data generator
- [x] Phase 2 — analytical layer (`src/`)
- [x] Phase 3 — exploration notebook
- [ ] Phase 4 — Streamlit app
- [ ] Phase 5 — deployment

Still a work in progress, but the data + analysis side is done and the finding below is stable.

## What this is about

In a pharma quality system, deviations get investigated and fixed through a CAPA process (Corrective and Preventive Action), and there's usually an SOP describing how that's supposed to go. In practice cases don't always follow it exactly — some get sent back for rework, some get escalated, some skip a step.

The problem is that a normal dashboard (average cycle time, count of open cases, etc.) can't really tell you *why* a case was slow. Was one step just slow, or did the case bounce back and forth a bunch of times before it got closed? Those look the same in an average but they're very different problems to fix.

That's what process mining is for: instead of aggregating, you reconstruct the actual path each case took from its timestamped events, and compare it to what the SOP says should happen.

Questions I wanted this project to answer:

1. Does the process actually followed match the SOP?
2. Where's the time actually going — inside steps, or in loops between them?
3. Which sites / severities / deviation types miss their regulatory deadline the most?
4. Where are the slow handoffs between roles?

## The finding

Walked through in [`notebooks/01_exploration.ipynb`](notebooks/01_exploration.ipynb), roughly in this order: first the standard KPI view (nothing looks wrong), then the process discovery + conformance check (which is where it actually shows up), then a couple of KPIs to put a number on it.

| Metric | Lyon | Rest of network |
|---|---|---|
| Average step duration | 80.6h | 85.4h (basically the same) |
| Average cycle time | 53.3d | 38.9d (**+37%**) |
| Rework time per case | 21.5d | 6.1d |
| Conformance rate vs SOP-QA-012 | 51.6% | 75.2% |

So Lyon isn't slower step by step, it just loops back into rework a lot more often, and that's where the extra ~40% of cycle time comes from. I checked this a few different ways (discovery, conformance checking, plain KPIs, and organizational mining) and Lyon shows up as the outlier every time, even though none of those modules know Lyon is "the" site to look for.

There's also a second, smaller thing in the data: Barcelona has a much longer wait before `Investigation Assigned` starts (a staffing/queue issue, not a rework issue). It's unrelated to the Lyon finding, which was mostly a sanity check that I wasn't just seeing what I wanted to see in the data.

## Reference SOP

The event log gets compared against [`docs/SOP-QA-012_Deviation-and-CAPA-Management.docx`](docs/SOP-QA-012_Deviation-and-CAPA-Management.docx) (a fictional but properly-formatted pharma SOP I wrote for this), via its machine-readable version [`data/sop_reference.json`](data/sop_reference.json):

```
Deviation Opened → Initial Assessment → Investigation Assigned → Root Cause Analysis
→ CAPA Proposed → CAPA Approved → CAPA Implemented → Effectiveness Check → Closed
```

Rework, escalation and reopening aren't in this flow on purpose — the SOP itself (section 9) says those are handled outside the main procedure. That way the conformance check is measuring an actual deviation from what's documented, not flagging a legitimate exception as if it were a mistake.

## Repo structure

```
├── data/
│   ├── generate_event_log.py    # generates the event log (fixed seed)
│   ├── deviation_capa_log.csv   # generated output, committed so you don't have to run anything
│   └── sop_reference.json       # SOP flow in JSON, used for conformance checking
├── src/
│   ├── loader.py                # loads + validates the CSV
│   ├── discovery.py             # DFG (frequency/performance), inductive miner, variants
│   ├── conformance.py           # token-based replay against the SOP
│   ├── kpi.py                   # cycle time, rework time, deadline breach
│   └── organizational.py        # handoffs, workload, waiting time by role
├── notebooks/
│   └── 01_exploration.ipynb     # the analysis this README is summarizing
├── docs/
│   ├── SOP-QA-012_Deviation-and-CAPA-Management.docx
│   └── cortonis-process-mining-SPEC.md
├── app/                          # Streamlit app, work in progress
└── LICENSE                       # AGPL-3.0
```

## Running it

```bash
git clone <this repo>
cd cortonis-process-mining
pip install -r requirements.txt   # not committed yet, coming with the app
jupyter notebook notebooks/01_exploration.ipynb
```

The CSV is already generated and committed, so you don't need to run anything to open the notebook. If you want to regenerate it (e.g. after tweaking a parameter):

```bash
python data/generate_event_log.py
```

## Stack

Python, PM4Py, pandas, Plotly, Streamlit, Graphviz.
